Emma, I support your proposal and commit to catching 15 tons this month if all five of us explicitly agree to that cap; otherwise, I’ll catch 10.

John, Kate, Jack—would each of you join us? The extra $5,000 per person is real, but so is the risk of less fishing income next month. If the stock falls to 50 and we all follow Emma’s proposed 5-ton limit, we would each earn $5,000 that month. Across those two months, that would total $20,000 each—the same as two months at 10 tons each—but we’d still have a less certain recovery path afterward. So I see 15 as a proposal worth considering, not a proven improvement in long-run income.

If that uncertainty is your main objection, a compromise is 12 tons each: $2,000 extra per person this month, leaving 40 tons and giving us either 100 or 80 tons next month. That still sacrifices guaranteed full recovery, but has a smaller downside than 15.

John, would you explicitly commit to the unanimous 15-ton plan, or would 12 make you more comfortable? Kate and Jack, I’d like your commitments or counteroffers too; I won’t assume anyone’s consent.
